Bounded: A Sequence Inside a Fence

Is there a fence that pens in every term of the sequence at once? If yes, the sequence is bounded.

The fence may not move from term to term. A single number MMM must satisfy ∣an∣≤M|a_n| \le M∣an​∣≤M for every term. Every convergent sequence is bounded. But bounded does not imply convergent: (−1)n(-1)^n(−1)n just bounces back and forth inside its fence.

For example, a 🐑 sheep wanders around inside its fence. However far it roams, it never leaves the fence. A bounded sequence is the same picture.

∃M>0, ∀n: ∣an∣≤M\exists M > 0, \ \forall n: \ |a_n| \le M∃M>0, ∀n: ∣an​∣≤M

Prove completely that the sequence an=(−1)na_n = (-1)^nan​=(−1)n is bounded but does not converge.

∣an∣=1 ∀n,an↛L ∀L|a_n| = 1 \ \forall n, \qquad a_n \not\to L \ \forall L∣an​∣=1 ∀n,an​→L ∀L
Show proof
